beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: More Words Than Reality examines research that looks mature before independent checks justify it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The problem extends beyond fabricated facts to convincing architectures, tests, and validation packages.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book separates perceived achievement from what survives comparison, execution, and attempted falsification.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It proposes tools for checking knowledge claims while preserving explicit human responsibility for value judgments.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers gain a framework for challenging apparent progress without dismissing useful AI-assisted research.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A theory can arrive with diagrams, code, tests, and a persuasive review of itself.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Those artifacts may still address a nearby problem rather than the intended one.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A new vocabulary can also conceal resemblance to earlier work.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book calls attention to what remains after relevant independent checks.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its concern is the gap between apparent maturity and a contribution that withstands scrutiny.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A proposed research system would record whether a statement is assumed, tested, or demonstrated.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Source checks, execution, baselines, and counterexamples would challenge different aspects of the claim.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book also separates evidential assessment from decisions about what is worth pursuing.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These guardian architectures are research proposals, not established machines for certifying discovery.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their own evaluation must resist the circular validation they are designed to expose.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin with the taxonomy of illusions and its concrete tests of apparent progress.
